messages:
alexandra: noticing spikes in east-west latency and repeated NIC resets on a small cohort of p4d.24xlarge nodes in us-east-1 starting ~01:42 UTC; monitoring-bot alerted about interface flaps and huge tx_retries.
monitoring-bot: alert: interface_flap detected on eni-0d4e5f6a- p4d-24xlarge cluster: training-gpu-east. metric spike: tx_retries > 1000 in 5m window.
rick: which kernel/driver versions are those nodes running? any recent AMI rollouts?
alexandra: these are on ami-ml-2026-02-10 + kernel 6.2.10-rt; ena module v2.11.0 and ena FW reported v1.3.7 by ethtool -i. No AMI changes in past 3 days.
nina: can you paste ethtool -S ens2f1 and dmesg tail?
alexandra: ethtool -S ens2f1 \n```\nrx_errors: 3012\nrx_missed: 0\ntx_retries: 1248\ntx_queue_stop: 76\nrx_ring_overflow: 1291\n```\n...dmesg shows repeating: `ENA: descriptor bounce detected` and `eth0: NIC reset - recovery path` and periodic `NETDEV WATCHDOG: ens2f1`.
rick: "descriptor bounce" sounds like DMA/PCI mapping or firmware refusing descriptors under sustained burst. Are these nodes doing heavy NVLink/XLA traffic or lots of tiny packets east-west?
alexandra: yes, large all-reduce across GPUs + gRPC checkpoints -> many small messages. We also saw a correlation with MTU=9000 jumbo frames.
infra-bot: suggestion: try temporary mitigations: 1) disable large offloads (LRO/GRO/GSO/TSO) 2) reduce MTU to 1500 on canary nodes 3) set IRQ affinity to spread queues 4) avoid rmmod/modprobe on production if possible.
rick: let's pick one non-prod node from the same ASG and test. nina, can you run an experiment?
nina: taking node train-test-01 out of rotation. steps: (1) `ip link set ens2f1 mtu 1500` (2) `ethtool -K ens2f1 gso off gro off tso off lro off` (3) `echo 1 > /sys/module/ena/parameters/ena_disable_lro` (if param exists) (4) restart the app that uses RDMA fallback. Will monitor.
monitoring-bot: note: offload toggles and MTU changes may affect perf for bulk transfers. track throughput vs errors.
alexandra: after toggles on test node: tx_retries dropped from ~300/min to ~5/min within 90s; no more descriptor bounce messages in dmesg; packet latency normalized.
rick: good signal. That indicates offload/MTU interaction with driver/firmware. Could be a regression introduced in ena FW 1.3.7 or module 2.11.0 in combination with kernel 6.2.10-rt.
alexandra: started a small DaemonSet (selector: tag=p4d-east-flaky) to flip offloads on a canary pool of 8 nodes. Also added kube labels to exclude them from scale-up for non-latency-sensitive workloads.
rick: plan: 1) keep DaemonSet for immediate mitigation 2) open vendor case with AWS EC2/NIC team with dmesg, pci ids, ethtool -i/-S, capture pcap of failing flows 3) schedule controlled firmware downgrade on one dev instance (if possible) or pin enav module to 2.9 to reproduce 4) avoid mass rolling reboots until vendor confirms.
infra-bot: created ticket AWS-NE-89012 linking logs and sample core dumps.
alexandra: one oddity: some nodes show tx_queue_stop but low tx_errors; others show rx_ring_overflow without tx symptoms. Might be multi-symptom of same root cause.
nina: added `irqbalance` tuning and set `RPS` queues on canary: `echo 2048 > /sys/class/net/ens2f1/queues/rx-0/rps_cpus` etc. Observed marginal improvement.
rick: capture and attach `lspci -vvv` and `modinfo ena` plus `uname -a` to vendor ticket. Also request ENA FW version history and known issues for 1.3.x -> 1.4.x.
alexandra: note for runbook: do NOT enable MTU 9000 on affected hosts until vendor confirms. Also avoid live kernel module unloads on nodes running long-running training jobs.
monitoring-bot: temporary autoscale policy active: if tx_retries > 200 for 3m -> cordon + evict + spin up fallback instance-type (g5dn).
rick: next steps: vendor call tomorrow 16:00 UTC. Nina, please prepare a minimal repro using microbenchmarks (iperf with many small packets, grpc hammer) to run while vendor watches.
nina: will do. Also capturing perf counters and posting to ticket.
alexandra: summary: likely NIC driver/firmware mismatch causing descriptor/DMA churn under jittery small-packet east-west loads and jumbo frames. Mitigations applied: offload disable DaemonSet, MTU rollback on canaries, irq/RPS tuning, autoscale policy. Awaiting vendor analysis for definitive fix.
deploy-bot: incident-log: new incident created INC-9943 severity: P2 affected ASG: training-p4d-use1.
alexandra: I'll update once vendor suggests firmware or driver action. For now we're keeping the DaemonSet in place and avoiding further AMI or kernel changes on the ASG.
